steps.text: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook and stir onion in melted butter until softened, 7 to 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add egg noodles and cook, stirring occasionally, until partially cooked, about 5 minutes. Drain and return to the pot.

Pour onion mixture over noodles, then stir in cottage cheese, sour cream, salt, and pepper. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until sauce is heated through and noodles are tender, yet firm to the bite, 5 to 8 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Polish Noodles (Cottage Cheese and Noodles)
raw_recipe.description: This family-favorite recipe for pasta with cottage cheese, sour cream, and buttery sautéed onions can be served as either a main course or a side dish.

video.description: Buttery coated noodles with sour cream, cottage cheese, pepper, and salt. It’s all you need for this delicious dish!

review.reviewBody: It was a super easy, quick dish that tasted fantastic. I have it twice. The first time with egg noodles, and the second time I took another reviwer's suggestion and made it with wagon wheel noodles, which was the only pasta I had in the pantry at the time. Both ways turned out great. This is also a very kid friendly dish and is a nice alternative to the typical mac and cheese, which I can get burned out on.

I loved this recipe! I only made a couple changes. I added some garlic when I was sauteeing the onion. Then, because my pasta wasn't done yet, I thought I would add my cottage cheese to the onion in the skillet just to heat it up. Then, to my surprise, the cottage cheese melted into a smooth, creamy, cheesy sauce. Yum! I can't wait to try this again and add some sharp cheddar to make it more like macaroni and cheese and see what that's like. I also love the nutrition you get from all the protein in the cottage cheese! This is a keeper!

I loved this! I made it exactly as the recipe called for the first time, and then the second time I boiled the noodles in a big sauce pan and drained them after five minutes. I then sautéed the onions in the butter in the same pan I boiled the noodles. Make sure you cook the onions long enough. Otherwise you get crunchy bits. I stirred in the noodles, cottage cheese, sour cream, and cheese. I added garlic powder and a pinch of nutmeg, with lots of black pepper. Then I greases a large casserole dish and dumped everything in. I topped it with more shredded cheese and panko crumbs. I baked at 350 for an hour, checking it every 15 minutes. We like things crunchy around here so I let it brown and crisp op. Truly amazing, both ways. I’m looking forward to playing around with this one a lot.

I’m a casserole nut, I made the pasta in my instant pot. Sautéed the onions, and 2 tbsp chopped garlic. then added the SC and 24 Oz. of CC. Threw it all in a casserole, topped with smoked paprika and 4 oz cheddar, baked for 35 min and then broiled for 2!

Loved the simplicity. I made it for a crowd. Three 12 oz bags of egg noodles, 2-24oz containers small curd cottage cheese, 1-16 oz container sour cream, 1 cup diced onion, 2 sticks of butter and salt and pepper to taste. Cooked the noodles for 5 minutes. In a separate pan, I cooked the butter and onions then added the sour cream and cottage cheese. I heated it enough to get rid of most of the lumps. I put 1/3 the noodles in a large crock pot, followed by the onion/cheese mixture and I repeated this twice. Then stirred. Yummy. The leftovers will need extra cheese but it does taste like the cheese and onion pierogies. I would make this again.

We grew up on this! — and still make it! My parents used dry cottage cheese which is difficult to find today, and very expensive. Substitute Farmers Cheese, and add an 8oz bag of fine shredded Swiss cheese to the hot noodle mix! Stir onions, noodles and pasta together, cover and let the cheese flavors combine. I’m making it right now!

My family is Polish and Austrian and my mother made this all the time we used Pot Cheese, dry curd cottage cheese. I can't find it any longer so I use ricotta cheese and cream cheese. We add 2 eggs, cinnamon, sugar, golden raisins and bake it in a 9x13 greased pan. We call it Luchen Kugel. We eat it wam or room temperature.

This dish is now in a regular rotation in our home. We pretty much followed the recipe as written for the base of a full meal. We added cabbage, garlic, and thyme to the onion stage, sautéed them all down together. Then we increased the cottage cheese and sour cream portions to account for the cabbage addition. We're a Spam family (and proud of it, though we do use the low sodium version), and tossed that in toward the end of the process to warm through. We will likely start with the Spam at some point to get some char on it. We made this for friends who started out skeptical, but went back for healthy second portions.
We had this meal many times as a kid. The addition of buttered and crispy bread crumbs sprinkled on the top before baking, was what made it super good. Try it.

I grew up with cabbage and onion being sautéed in butter then adding it to the cottage cheese and hot noodles then it was baked 30 minutes. We had it with Kielbasa or pork roast as a side. Just made your way tonight, my kids don't like cabbage.

I enjoyed the dish very much but the next time I make it, I am going to add more sour cream. I thought it was a bit dry. I also, instead of finishing in the pot, mixed well and put it in a casserole. Baked, covered for 30 minutes at 400* .
I think this will be on the weekly rotation when I have to work late! Super yummy. Added some garlic with the onion and had warm sauerkraut on the side.
This turned out exactly how my great-grandma used to make it. It was pure nostalgia in a bowl. Highly recommend!
No followed the recipe ! Delicious !!!

Comfort food from my childhood. There was a cheese called pot cheese- it looked like cottage cheese- we used it for this- I don’t see it in supermarkets now. It’s still great recipe with cottage cheese!
So we would make this with elbow noodles and farmers cheese but have to say just made this version minus onion and sour cream always add lots of black pepper and yumm !

I come from a Polish family that made pierogies. My grandma could make her noodle dough so thin. She passed down the tradition to my mom. Of my mom's three kids I'm the only one to make pierogi and they are so time consuming! I will definitely try this "short cut" but will add some fresh cut chives to the dish as well for a nod to our family recipe.
Add a. Little bit. Of mozzarella and parmesean
Delicious! I added crumbled bacon when I sauteed the onions and it was great!
Awesome flavors and extremely fast and easy.
